test_title: PYST 22: SSC CHSL - English (Held On: 16 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, "I had gone to Shimla."

options.text: He said that he had gone to Shimla.
He said that he went to Shimla.
He says that he had gone to Shimla.
He said that he has gone to Shimla.

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct indirect form** of the given sentence "He said, 'I had gone to Shimla.'" is: "He said that he had gone to Shimla."
 
• **When converting direct speech** into indirect speech, the tense of the verb usually moves back into the past. This is known as 'backshifting'.
 
• However,** if the verb is already** in the past perfect tense ("had gone"), it remains in the past perfect tense in indirect speech.
 
• This is because the past perfect tense already represents an action that was completed before some point in the past, so there is no further 'past' tense to shift back to.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'He said that he had gone to Shimla.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are not correct:
 
 
• **"He said that he went to Shimla." -** The verb tense changes from past perfect ("had gone") to simple past ("went"), which is not consistent with the original sentence.
 
• **"He says that he had gone to Shimla." -** The verb in the reporting clause ("says") is in the present tense, whereas in the original sentence, it is in the past tense ("said").
 
• **"He said that he has gone to Shimla." - **The verb tense changes from past perfect ("had gone") to present perfect ("has gone"), which is not consistent with the original sentence.
